subject.title: feat: update Companion-owned Gateway safely in place

question: After the package-lifecycle dependency lands, should this large update-and-recovery feature be admitted only with a disposable full update-to-rollback proof for both normal native-backup protection and the explicit VHD path?
rationale: The branch’s safety claim is about a real WSL state transition and recovery boundary. Unit and coordinator tests do not establish that the installed Gateway can be updated and then recovered on the current composed runtime without losing the Companion-owned relationship.

options.title: Require full disposable recovery proof
options.body: Rebase after the dependency and require current-head live evidence for update, rollback or recovery, and post-recovery Gateway and node health before merge.

options.title: Accept narrower pre-merge proof
options.body: Accept native-backup and interruption evidence only, while explicitly deferring full rollback proof to a follow-up release gate.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Merge only a narrower version-detection and prompt seam, leaving protection, recovery, and retention for separately proven PRs.

recommendation.title: Require full disposable recovery proof
recommendation.body: Rebase after the dependency and require current-head live evidence for update, rollback or recovery, and post-recovery Gateway and node health before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The collaborator review already established the key product and operational constraint: routine update protection must be safe for ordinary storage capacity, not only technically recoverable.
